architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept adequate state control if S is less than or equal to 100.0%, equivalent to a maximum between-preparation viscosity-scale ratio exp(max(a_fr) - min(a_fr)) less than or equal to 2.00.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The primary observable does not depend on a rheological regularity previously measured in the same chemistry family as S1C41. S1C41 is unvalidated AC1920-plus-TK100-modified chemistry, but M-REPEAT directly measures repeated 80-130 C sweeps in that chemistry and does not transfer the unmodified-family thermal-response shape. The result can establish formulation-level realization reproducibility, not a molecular mechanism or modifier-specific causation.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If S is greater than 100.0%—equivalently, if the maximum between-preparation viscosity-scale ratio exceeds 2.00—the state-control premise required for interpreting candidate-to-core level differences is falsified. This outcome does not by itself falsify H-LEVEL-DILUTE, H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or H-LEVEL-PLASTIC; it makes their adjudication from an unmatched realization invalid. If S is less than or equal to 100.0%, none of the three registered level hypotheses is falsified because M-REPEAT measures state spread rather than selecting among their level predictions.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Resolve and fully record the six missing process-history fields, tighten preparation controls, and rerun S1C41::M-REPEAT until the maximum between-preparation viscosity-scale ratio is less than or equal to 2.00; do not adjudicate the registered level hypotheses or proceed to a drift claim while the ratio remains above 2.00.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Between-preparation viscosity-scale spread for at least three independently prepared S1C41 realizations, quantified as S = 100 * [exp(max(a_fr) - min(a_fr)) - 1] percent from the replicated 80-130 C sweeps.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41::M-REPEAT is admissible under the binding chemistry audit and directly targets the largest demonstrated interpretability defect: multi-fold preparation-state variation. It provides replicated direct sweeps in the modified chemistry without assuming unverified shape transfer. The three registered level hypotheses remain entangled, and thermal-hold mitigation remains unmeasured, but controlling realization state is the scientifically necessary prerequisite before either can be interpreted.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer on measurement choice. The Proposer's S1C41::M-SWEEP is top-ranked and nominally separates the frozen predictions, but its single preparation is not interpretable against an unspecified unmodified reference when E2 realization displacement is 2.80-3.57-fold, far above the asserted 3.40% level threshold. I retain the Proposer's S1C41 candidate because it is the smallest modifier burden in the tied top set, but select the Robustness Adjudicator's S1C41::M-REPEAT to remove the more fundamental state ambiguity. This experiment does not test the E5-type 120 C hold drift.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: There are no local measurements for the AC1920-plus-TK100 chemistry, the external-prior queries returned no rows, and the dual-axis formulation cannot isolate acrylic, TK100, interaction, or dilution-model contributions. M-REPEAT also lacks a contemporaneous unmodified E2 control.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Temperature extrapolation is avoided because viscosity is directly measured from 80 to 130 C. Chemistry extrapolation remains for any later comparison with the frozen level predictions, but it does not undermine the directly observed between-preparation spread.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The catalog supplies a 100.0% discrimination threshold for state control, but no modified-chemistry repeatability error smaller than that threshold. The 3.40% M-SWEEP residual is not used as repeatability precision for this experiment.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: This is the dominant uncertainty: unmodified E2 preparations showed CV values of 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C. Three independent S1C41 preparations directly estimate whether that displacement has been reduced.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The shared local temperature-response regularity was measured primarily in the original unmodified reactive-core PUR chemistry represented by E1-E3, with E2 as the candidate-space reactive-core anchor; E1 +P is a separate chemical-perturbation check rather than part of the primary same-composition fit. An experiment using nonzero acrylic-like or minor tackifier-like modifier would not remain strictly inside that measured chemistry family, so the shared shape must not be assumed without an applicability audit; absent support, a direct 80-130 C sweep is required.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive isothermal viscosity growth during hot residence at 120 C, creating a thermal-hold stability risk.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 hold increased by SI_15_60 = 0.5154 (51.5%) and SI_15_90 = 0.9308 (93.1%) at 120 C, versus 9.5% and 16.8%, respectively, for E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only E1 and E5 have original 120 C hold trajectories, each represented by one run over 15-90 min. E5 shows severe drift, but there are no independent repeats and no hold measurements for the prospective modified candidate space. By comparison, temperature response was measured at six temperatures from 80-130 C for multiple E1-E3 runs.
measurement_requirements: Use a candidate with nonzero modifier loading, because the unmodified reactive-core option has no differential prediction and cannot separate the registered level hypotheses.

Directly measure viscosity at 120 and 130 C, preferably within a fresh-sample 80-130 C sweep, so processing-window level and temperature response are observed rather than extrapolated across a chemistry change.

Compare the measured processing-temperature level with the frozen inert-dilution prediction using the applicable measurement-resolution threshold; classify agreement, elevation, or depression without assigning a molecular mechanism from rheology alone.
Run a matched-window 120 C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min with at least two independent repeats and report SI_15_60, so the E5-type residence-time drift is tested directly.
Control and record preparation and process history, because E2 nominal runs show CV values of 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C.
Preserve the unknown source viscosity unit and restrict conclusions to measured temperature and time windows.
planner.scientific_question: For a nonzero modifier loading, is the directly measured 120-130 C viscosity level consistent with inert reactive-mass dilution, elevated above that prediction by an acrylic-like contribution, or depressed below it by plasticization, while avoiding the large 120 C hold drift observed for E5?

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is resin-modified AC1920 plus TK100 chemistry outside the family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured. M-SWEEP is nevertheless admissible under the binding audit because it directly measures the processing-window level and establishes the response shape for this chemistry rather than transferring the unverified local shape.
hypotheses_not_separated: None among the registered level hypotheses; however, this experiment does not separate thermal-hold drift hypotheses or directly test the E5-type residence-time failure mode.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: A 120-130 C level change within 3.40 percentage points of exactly one frozen prediction supports that formulation-level hypothesis for S1C41: -42.76% supports H-LEVEL-DILUTE, +17.24% supports H-LEVEL-ASSOC, or -72.76% supports H-LEVEL-PLASTIC. This classifies the level response without establishing a molecular mechanism.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: H-LEVEL-DILUTE is falsified if the measured change differs from -42.76% by more than 3.40 percentage points. H-LEVEL-ASSOC is falsified if the change is at or below -42.76%, while H-LEVEL-PLASTIC is falsified if it is at or above -42.76%. Thus a result on either side of the inert-dilution prediction can falsify the opposing directional hypothesis even if it does not accept another prediction.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result outside all three 3.40-point acceptance neighborhoods, inconsistent between 120 and 130 C, or otherwise not uniquely assignable would leave the registered level hypotheses unresolved for this realization and indicate an unmodelled modifier contribution and/or process-state displacement. It would not answer whether 120 C hold drift was mitigated.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured viscosity level from 80 to 130 C, with the 120 and 130 C levels compared against the unmodified reactive core; apparent E_eta from ln(eta) versus 1/T is a secondary fitted descriptor.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Identical deterministic VOI and full pairwise discrimination, but its 17.5 wt% acrylic loading creates a larger chemistry perturbation than S1C41 without adding hypothesis separation.

Identical deterministic VOI and stronger directly commensurate acrylic analogue support near 20 wt%, but it imposes a larger total modifier burden when the 15 wt% design already separates all registered predictions.
Identical deterministic VOI and in-region composition, but 22.5 wt% acrylic is a larger departure from the measured local chemistry with no additional discrimination.
Identical deterministic VOI and direct support at 25 wt% acrylic, but it is the largest chemistry perturbation in the tied set and offers no additional registered-hypothesis separation.

It directly addresses the declared thermal-hold failure mode and is the necessary follow-up for drift, but it does not resolve the processing-window level or separate any of the three registered level hypotheses.

proposer.reasoning: The binding chemistry audit excludes one-point shape-transfer anchors for resin-modified candidates, making a direct sweep the appropriate admissible measurement. S1C41::M-SWEEP directly observes 120-130 C viscosity, establishes the previously unverified thermal response of the modified chemistry, lies inside both external intervention regions, and separates all three registered hypothesis pairs at 3.40% resolution. The principal limitation is moderate process-state risk and the absence of a hold trajectory; therefore this experiment determines level behavior but cannot establish mitigation of the E5-type 120 C drift.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards directly measure the decision quantity, separate all three hypothesis pairs, and remain within both externally supported modifier regions. S1C41 uses the smallest sufficient modifier burden in the tied set: 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier and 5 wt% minor tackifier-like modifier. This minimizes departure from the characterized reactive-core chemistry while retaining full discrimination; 5 wt% TK100 lies in the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, and 15 wt% AC1920 lies at the declared lower boundary of the supported acrylic region.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed the measurement from the single-preparation S1C41::M-SWEEP to S1C41::M-REPEAT so that between-preparation state displacement is measured using at least three independently prepared realizations. The candidate remains S1C41 because it is the smallest modifier burden in the tied top set. The change does not authorize use of the 3.40% threshold as candidate-versus-core repeatability, does not isolate AC1920 from TK100, and does not test thermal-hold drift.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: The proposal S1C41::M-SWEEP is in the five-card tied top set, but the preferred experiment departs from that ranking to S1C41::M-REPEAT. The departure is justified by measured E2 realization variability of 2.80-3.57-fold across 80-130 C, which is far larger than the asserted 3.40% discrimination threshold. M-REPEAT uses at least three independently prepared S1C41 realizations and directly measures an 80-130 C sweep for each, making preparation-state variability estimable before formulation-level prediction regions are interpreted.
residual_decision_risk: M-REPEAT does not include a contemporaneous matched unmodified E2 preparation, so candidate-to-core level change and its uncertainty remain incompletely specified.
The 3.40% threshold comes from a shared-shape regression residual and is not established as repeatability or comparison error for AC1920-plus-TK100 chemistry.
S1C41 changes AC1920 and TK100 simultaneously, leaving acrylic-specific, tackifier-specific, interaction, and dilution-model effects causally entangled.
No selected hold measurement observes SI_15_60, so mitigation of the E5-type 120 C residence-time drift remains unresolved.
Six process fields remain missing; uncontrolled process history may continue to contribute to realization displacement.
Directional falsification at the inert-dilution boundary requires an uncertainty margin and should not be applied to values experimentally indistinguishable from that boundary.

The resin-modified chemistry is outside the family supporting the prior shared thermal-response regularity; direct replicated sweeps remain valid, but unverified shape transfer and molecular-mechanism claims remain inadmissible.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection undermines the interpretability of the proposed single S1C41 sweep rather than merely qualifying a secondary descriptor. Because the decision statistic is a candidate-to-unmodified-core level change, a single uncontrolled realization can move among the frozen prediction regions for reasons unrelated to formulation. S1C41::M-REPEAT is therefore preferred as the available card that directly addresses preparation-state variability while retaining replicated 80-130 C sweeps. This does not fully solve the problem because its protocol lacks a contemporaneous matched E2 reference. The five-way deterministic tie also does not justify moving to a higher modifier loading: all tied cards leave the acrylic and TK100 effects entangled, so S1C41 remains the least-burden candidate among them, but its result cannot establish modifier-specific causation.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: No tested perturbation changed the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0 across all 29 scenarios, and every weight term survived scaling from 0.5 to 1.5 with no recommendation_flip_boundary. The base margin to the first strictly lower card was 0.002292. Thus no perturbation within the reported sweep makes the proposal cease to be top ranked. Weightings outside the tested range were not evaluated. The departure is not caused by re-weighting; it addresses an observable-design defect that the score does not adequately encode, namely that a single candidate realization cannot support a 3.40% candidate-to-core discrimination claim when the reference system exhibits multi-fold realization displacement.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary 120 C and 130 C viscosity levels stay inside measured support because M-SWEEP measures them directly on S1C41 and establishes the modified chemistry's own temperature response; it does not transfer the unmodified-family shape. Before claiming 3.40% discrimination precision, the modified chemistry and its comparison with the unmodified core require independent preparations or a contemporaneous matched reference to establish actual repeatability.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: Direct measurements at 120 C and 130 C can fall on either side of -42.76% or more than 3.40 percentage points from it, so the stated criteria can be met. However, association and plasticization use a zero-margin directional boundary despite 3.40% declared resolution, and the one-preparation protocol does not establish that an apparent departure is larger than realization-state uncertainty.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Agreement with -42.76%, +17.24%, or -72.76% could be reported as hypothesis discrimination even though the observed level difference may reflect unmatched realization state or the unisolated tackifier axis.
objections.objection: The three frozen predictions for S1C41 are numerically separated by 30 to 90 percentage points, well above the declared 3.40% threshold, so nominal pairwise separation survives. Practical separation does not: M-SWEEP has min_repeats = 1 and does not control realization state, while the E2 reference has measured CV values of 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios of 2.80-3.57 across 80-130 C. A single candidate realization compared with an unspecified prior unmodified reference can therefore move among the prediction regions because of preparation-state displacement rather than formulation response. In addition, the proposal declares that no registered level hypotheses remain unseparated, although the acrylic-specific contribution in H-LEVEL-ASSOC remains entangled with the simultaneous 5 wt% TK100 change and any AC1920-by-TK100 interaction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment may classify one dual-modifier formulation against three numerical prediction rules, but it cannot support causal attribution to acrylic association, joint plasticization, or either modifier axis separately.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes at once: AC1920 is 15 wt% and TK100 is 5 wt%, while the reactive core falls to 80 wt%. The experiment contains no acrylic-only, TK100-only, or contemporaneous unmodified control. Consequently, an elevated viscosity cannot be attributed specifically to the acrylic-like axis, and a depressed viscosity cannot distinguish joint plasticization from a TK100-only effect, an AC1920-only effect, dilution-model error, or an AC1920-by-TK100 interaction. The same protocol also leaves six process fields missing and has process_state_risk = 0.75.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The reported percentage change and its 3.40-point acceptance neighborhood may appear more precise and more directly observed than the protocol supports.
objections.objection: The 120 C and 130 C viscosities are directly measured by M-SWEEP, and the proposer correctly treats E_eta as a secondary fitted descriptor. However, the primary decision statistic is the percentage change 'against the unmodified reactive core,' not merely the raw viscosity. The protocol does not specify a contemporaneous matched E2 preparation, how the highly variable E2 reference level will be selected, or how uncertainty in that baseline enters the comparison. Thus the raw candidate levels are direct, but the claimed relative level change is not a fully specified matched-window observable. The 3.40% threshold also comes from a shared-shape-plus-intercept regression residual, not from repeatability of the proposed candidate-versus-reference comparison.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct viscosity measurements remain valid, but the claimed 3.40% discrimination precision may be transferred beyond the evidence that established it.
objections.objection: The proposed primary measurement survives this attack surface. S1C41 is outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry family, but M-SWEEP directly measures 80-130 C and does not reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity using the unverified shared shape. The proposal therefore does not reuse the unmodified-family thermal-response shape as evidence for the primary level. The remaining limitation is that the declared 3.40% discrimination resolution was derived from a shared-shape fit and has not been independently verified as the repeatability or comparison error for AC1920-plus-TK100 chemistry.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result too close to the dilution boundary to resolve experimentally could be presented as falsifying a directional hypothesis.
objections.objection: The protocol can numerically produce results satisfying the stated falsification rules, so the criterion is attainable. Nevertheless, the directional criteria for H-LEVEL-ASSOC and H-LEVEL-PLASTIC use the exact -42.76% dilution boundary with no 3.40% uncertainty margin: association is called falsified at or below -42.76%, and plasticization at or above -42.76%. Values within measurement resolution of that boundary therefore trigger formal falsification despite being experimentally indistinguishable from it. Single-preparation state uncertainty further weakens practical falsification.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment could be treated as evidence that the E5-type residence-time failure was mitigated or that acrylic association occurred, although neither conclusion is measured.
objections.objection: No target wet-lab outcome or validation-formulation identity is exposed in the supplied trace, so direct outcome leakage is not demonstrated. The scope mismatch is substantive: the planner's scientific question includes 'avoiding the large 120 C hold drift observed for E5,' and the declared failure mode is excessive isothermal viscosity growth, but S1C41::M-SWEEP has no hold times and cannot measure SI_15_60. The proposer admits this limitation. Also, rheology on the dual-axis formulation cannot establish the molecular-sounding assertion that the acrylic-like component 'associates within the melt'; at most it can show that the formulation-level viscosity lies above a frozen numerical prediction.

skeptic.recommended_change: Retain the direct M-SWEEP but run at least three independent S1C41 preparations under fully recorded process histories and include contemporaneous matched unmodified E2 sweeps so the candidate-to-core level change and its uncertainty are directly estimable. If the stated scientific question remains mitigation of E5-type drift, also run the available S1C41::M-HOLD-120 protocol with at least two independent repeats at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min. To make modifier-axis attribution, use available single-axis controls rather than relying only on the dual-axis formulation.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The single, uncontrolled S1C41 sweep is compared against an unspecified unmodified reference despite E2 realization variability of 2.80-3.57-fold. That state displacement is far larger than the asserted 3.40% discrimination resolution and can make the candidate-versus-reference level change uninterpretable.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
